Call notes — Priya Raghavan, Ashford Home Furnishings (Tue)

Two sides to the business and she wants them funded separately, not blended.
The retail showroom side is the bread and butter: consumers in the market for
furniture, mostly homeowners doing a room or two at a time. The trade side is
interior designers and home stagers buying on behalf of their own clients —
far fewer people, much higher ticket, and she's been trying to grow it for two
years without much to show for it.

Split the budget 60/40, retail taking the 60. Same product on both sides,
she's not looking for anything clever — just straight Premion streaming
against each group. $80,000 for the campaign.

March through May. DC metro only — three showrooms inside the beltway and she
doesn't want to pay to reach anyone past that.

No agency involved, she buys direct. Asked us to keep the two sides clearly
separated on the plan so she can see what each one is getting.
